verification.note: file_question.py:1050-1056: `page` (and `pixmap` if tobytes raises) are bound before the `del pixmap, page` at 1056, which only runs on success. On a raise, _locked's finally (1082-1083) releases PYMUPDF_LOCK as the exception leaves the with block; the image() frame stays alive via exc.__traceback__. rag.py:2346-2350 catches it as `except Exception as exc: unavailable(...)`; the implicit `del exc` at the end of that handler frees the traceback, the frame and `page`, with no lock held. Whether a given PyMuPDF Page finalizer actually calls into MuPDF was not checked against the installed library.

file_question.py:1060 binds a local `document` in close(); 1066 calls _close_locked(document, acquired=True), whose `del document` (1011) removes only its own parameter binding, and its finally releases the lock (1013). close()'s local drops the last reference when close() returns, after the release. In the thread branch (1070-1072), CPython's Thread.run holds the Document in self._args until its own finally deletes _target/_args, after _close_locked returned and released the lock. So the Document is always deallocated outside the lock, although close() itself does run under it.

unspecified_scores.reason: It happens only when a page request runs out of its 30 s lock budget during a long PDF extraction, and the only effect is a file handle that a background thread keeps open until the extraction finishes; the user sees nothing.
An EPUB or PDF section title longer than 60 characters with a space at the cut point gives a contents line with a double space before ' — '; only the model sees it, and nothing changes for the user.
A stored title made only of citation-like markers or whitespace hardly ever occurs in real documents, and the line simply reads like an untitled section.

specification_compliance: I8: render and close calls run inside PYMUPDF_LOCK, but finalizers of Page/Pixmap on the failure path and the Document's deallocation run outside it (CR7-1, CR7-2 confirmed). Whether this breaks I8 depends on whether a finalizer counts as a 'PyMuPDF call made to render page images'.
regression_risks: Concurrent MuPDF object deallocation outside PYMUPDF_LOCK during a page-render failure or after close, at the same time as an extraction thread that holds the lock.
test_coverage: test_a_page_that_fails_to_render_takes_no_number_and_the_others_close_up exercises the raise path but does not check where the Page is freed relative to the lock.
The hygiene test checks that Document.close runs under the lock, but not where the Document is deallocated.
not_verified: Whether the installed PyMuPDF version's Page, Pixmap or Document __del__ actually call into MuPDF, or are no-ops after close.
No code was run; the reference lifetimes were traced by reading the code and from CPython semantics (implicit del of the except variable, Thread.run's finally).
Other invariants (I1-I7, I9) were not re-reviewed.
